I teach political behaviour, political communication, and quantitative methods. My aim in
the classroom is that students leave able to *do* something — read a study critically,
pull their own data, and defend a design — rather than only recognise a literature.

::: {.note-box}
**Currently supervising?** I am happy to supervise BA and MA theses on political
communication, social media and politics, misinformation, and quantitative political
behaviour. [Email me](mailto:madshove@ps.au.dk) with a paragraph on what you want to
study, or [book an office-hours slot](office-hours.qmd).
:::

## Thesis supervision

I supervise theses that use quantitative or computational methods on questions about
political communication and behaviour. Topics I am well placed to supervise include:

- Political advertising and microtargeting on social platforms
- Misinformation, AI-generated content, and how audiences evaluate it
- Politicians' and parties' communication strategies
- Comment sections and online political discussion
- Descriptive and measurement-focused projects on Danish politics

A good starting point is a question you can actually get data on. If you are unsure
whether that is the case for your idea, bring it to office hours — that is often the
fastest way to find out.
